title: MCP SDK upgrade + July 2026 spec adoption (stdio)
summary: Investigate upgrading @modelcontextprotocol/sdk past the 1.22.0 pin (1.30.0 types OOM tsc with zod 3.25 — find the fixed version or migration path, e.g. zod v4). Review the July 2026 MCP spec revision for capabilities usable by our stdio server (brainfile mcp). Deliverable: upgrade landed with compile-time check + spec features worth adopting, validated.

title: Thin-frontend refactor: move V2 domain logic from cli to core
summary: Discovery complete (single-agent Sonnet workflow). Core is rich for the dead V1 architecture but thin for live V2 — every V2 mutation (move/patch/subtask/complete orchestration, ranked search) is hand-rolled independently in CLI commands, MCP tools, and TUI actions, producing real behavioral drift: TUI move skips auto-complete-on-completionColumn (CLI+MCP do it); MCP subtask tool uses a different ID algorithm than the CLI; 4-5 inconsistent search rankers. 67 modules classified: 14 move-to-core, 12 split, 2 dead, 39 stay. 14 duplications (some verbatim copies of existing core exports). Full spec with 6 implementation phases: .brainfile/plans/2026-08-11-cli-core-boundary-spec.md — Phase 0 (dead code) and Phase 1 (boilerplate consolidation) are near-zero risk; Phase 2 (V2 file-mutation core layer) is the structural fix that also kills the drift bugs.

title: First-class plans: document type, linkage, and verbs
summary: Promote .brainfile/plans/ from informal agent convention to a first-class document type. The flexible types system nearly covers it already (types: {plan: {idPrefix: plan}}); what's missing: (1) canonical location + naming (plans/ dir vs board/ with type=plan), (2) IDs (plan-N) and frontmatter schema (title, status, related tasks — parentId links any-to-any today), (3) CLI/MCP verbs: plan add/list/show/link, (4) agents discovering plans relevant to a task (task -> plan backlink), (5) search across plan bodies. Design constraint: build on the V2 file-mutation core layer (spec-2 Phase 2) so all frontends see plans identically.

title: TUI v3: ink 7 platform jump + dense clarity-focused redesign
summary: Approved: upgrade ink and redesign simultaneously. Design authority: .brainfile/plans/2026-08-12-tui-v3-design-spec.md — dense one-row-per-document list with type glyphs and signal-only color, context footer, split/full detail, / filter backed by core searchTasksRanked, ink 7 + react 19 via esbuild-bundled CLI (resolves task-7 for the TUI path; yoga-wasm handling and jest/ESM test strategy bound by scope agent). View-layer swap over unchanged actions — parity suites must stay green. Built via scope/build/verify workflow.

title: brainfile brief: the agent session-start verb
summary: Decision (George): brief only — inbox killed as a subsystem (board + notes + recoil already cover lateral communication; today's multi-agent session needed zero DMs). Tripwire for ever revisiting messaging: agents writing notes aimed at a specific other agent on tasks that agent isn't assigned to. instruct and note --agent provenance bolt on later.

title: TUI v3.1: collapse/expand, type-cycle views, detail v2
summary: George's desktop feedback, decisions locked: flat cursor, expanded by default, type-cycle for plan/type views. Binding spec: .brainfile/plans/2026-08-12-tui-v3.1-spec.md — Part A: spacebar collapse/expand with glyph rotation + N-hidden chip + persisted collapsed set in state/tui.json; t type-cycle composing with / filter. Part B: detail v2 — breadcrumb drill-down through children, real contract block, activity tail (core parseLogEntries export), u/d body scrolling replacing silent truncation, flat cursor over child+subtask stops, p to parent. Sonnet builds; Claude validates directly (no verify agent).

title: TUI audit: rules removal (adr-2), panel collapse, rubric fixes
summary: Final UI/UX audit pass before 0.20.0. Yardstick: plans/2026-08-12-tui-rubric.md (10 first-principles tests). Binding spec: plans/2026-08-12-tui-audit-spec.md — A: rules system removed per adr-2 (schema, lint --fix folds into agent.instructions, commands/rules.ts deleted, core rule ops removed — authorized breaking removals, adr promote simplified, brief shows instructions + accepted ADRs); B: 1/2/3 panels collapsed — completed history becomes a done stop on the t type-cycle with read-only gating; C: $EDITOR handoff replacing all inline editing, NO_COLOR, resume last column/type, live-refresh cursor-survival guarantee, cold-start guard, h/l keybinds; D: hygiene sweep.

title: MCP tools: adopt 2026-07-28 structured output + list caching
summary: Now that we're on SDK v2 / spec 2026-07-28: our 10 tools return JSON stringified into text content. Adopt outputSchema + structuredContent so agents get typed results instead of parsing strings; set honest ttlMs/cacheScope on list_tasks/search results; consider icons metadata (SEP-973) for tool listings. Small effort, direct agent-experience win, rides the fresh SDK.

title: Completions never write ledger.jsonl — legacyMode everywhere
summary: Found while verifying brief: complete.ts:74, task_complete_tool.ts:60, and moveTaskFileToColumn's auto-complete all pass legacyMode: true, so buildLedgerRecord/appendLedgerRecord never run — .brainfile/logs/ledger.jsonl doesn't exist and core warns 'falling back to legacy markdown logs' on every ledger read. The board's agent instructions even claim completions are 'recorded in ledger.jsonl'. Decide: dual-write (ledger record AND archived markdown — likely right: ledger for queries, markdown for humans) or fix the default. Affects brief's completion lane, log/search over history, and getTaskContext.

title: Revisit @modelcontextprotocol/sdk pin (1.22.0)
summary: SDK 1.30.0 types OOM tsc (>12GB) against zod 3.25 — pinned exactly 1.22.0 in cli/package.json. Watch upstream releases; upgrade needs a compile-memory check (npx tsc in cli/ should stay seconds, not minutes).

summary: npm outdated + npm audit across the workspace; apply upgrades that fix vulnerabilities or meaningful staleness without churn. Validate with full build + 782 tests. MCP SDK excluded — tracked separately.

title: CLIError renders as raw stack trace instead of clean usage message
summary: Repro: run 'brainfile complete task-5' (missing --task flag). Expected: one-line error + usage. Actual: full CLIError stack trace thrown through yoga-layout nbind.js. CLIError carries exitCode and details but nothing catches it at the top level in dist/cli.js — add a top-level catch that prints message + details and exits with exitCode. Found while dogfooding 0.18.1.

summary: docs/guides/orchestration.md still documents @brainfile/supervisor / bfs commands — package is archived (private 1broseidon/brainfile-supervisor). Remove or rewrite the Automated Dispatch section; sweep for other supervisor/ACP mentions.

summary: chalk 6, chokidar 5, commander 15, open 11, ink 4+ (and react 18+) are all ESM-only; cli is CommonJS (module: commonjs). Decide: full ESM migration, or bundle (tsup/esbuild) and keep CJS entry. Unlocking ink 4+ matters most (TUI is on ink 3 + react 17). title: spec-9 phase 1: tracked storage, resolution, per-mutation commits, init/migrate
summary: BoardRepo git helper (cli/src/utils/board-repo.ts); core findBrainfile stopAtGitRoot; CLI resolution steps 3-4 (worktree list lookup, materialize from local or origin branch); pre/postAction commit hooks in cli.ts with hand edits committed as 'edit:'; MCP withBoardCommit wrapper on the 7 mutating tools; TUI debounced commits; init --tracked/--plain/--here/-g; migrate --to-branch (subtree split, standalone fold-in, orphan import) and --to-plain; tests with real git.

title: spec-9 phase 2: sync verb, remote config, gitattributes + merge driver, brief auto-sync
summary: brainfile sync [--pull|--push] [--set-remote <name|url>]: fetch, ff or merge --no-edit, push; git config brainfile.remote / brainfile.remoteBranch / brainfile.autosync; .gitattributes on the board branch (ledger merge=union, board/*.md merge=brainfile); 'brainfile merge-driver' field-level LWW + union of log lists; brief syncs first unless --offline; network failures are one-line warnings; tests with two clones and a bare remote.

title: spec-9 phase 3: autosync debounce, TUI sync indicator, MANUAL section, spec-5 re-scope, changelog
summary: Debounced background push after mutations when autosync=push|full; fetch-before-read in full mode; TUI header 'synced Ns ago'; MANUAL.md 'Sharing a board' section replacing the one-file-per-document justification; CHANGELOG Unreleased entry; spec-5 description updated to 'serve over the synced worktree'.

title: Board on a branch: shared board storage on a git ref
summary: Decision (George, 2026-09-21): the board becomes a linked git worktree on an orphan branch of the project repo, like gh-pages for tasks. Every mutation is one commit authored as the agent; sync is optional and targets a remote the user chooses, which may differ from the code remote so private boards can sit next to public code. Solves the actual sharing failure: board state versioned with code is stale per worktree and branch and invisible across machines; gitignored boards leave linked worktrees blind. Core stays git-free (task-9 boundary); commits and sync live in cli. Binding spec: .brainfile/plans/2026-09-21-board-on-a-branch-spec.md. Phase 1 (storage, resolution, per-mutation commits, migrate) ships same-machine sharing with zero sync; phase 2 adds sync, merge driver, brief auto-sync; phase 3 autosync, TUI indicator, MANUAL, spec-5 re-scope.

title: migrate --to-branch loses uncommitted board edits and leaves partial state on failure
summary: Reproduced 2026-09-22 with brainfile 0.20.0 on scratch repos (board committed on the code branch, the `trackedOnCodeBranch` path in migrateToBranch).

title: Store shared boards under refs/brainfile/ instead of a remote branch
summary: GitHub shows a 'had recent pushes / Compare & pull request' banner for every autosync push because the board is pushed to refs/heads/brainfile. Verified on a throwaway repo (1broseidon/brainfile-ref-test): a push to refs/brainfile/board is stored and fetchable but not a branch, so no banner, no branch list entry. Treat the remote as a free filestore.

title: Web board: first non-CLI frontend on browser-safe core
summary: Validate the thin-frontend platform with a real second frontend: minimal read-first web board (brainfile serve → local web UI, or static export). core already ships a browser-safe entrypoint (Apr 2026). Reuses the V2 mutation layer + searchTasksRanked + realtime diffing (diffBoards/hashBoard were built for exactly this). Scope decision: read-only viewer vs mutating app; local server vs hosted. After inbox design, unless it becomes the demo vehicle for relaunch.

title: Related boards: name sister repos, dependsOn across them, list them
summary: Boards can name sister boards in other repos so a task can point at one. Writing to a sister needs nothing new: the CLI and MCP tools already work in that repo's own directory. So the scope is only awareness, cross-repo dependsOn, and listing.

title: Triage marketing board
summary: marketing/.brainfile has 9 March-era idea tasks (stale HN/tweet references, but reusable angles: competitor positioning, context amnesia, AGENTS.md-but-structured) plus 2 Remotion video tasks in review. Re-anchor angles to the new tool-first positioning (no more 'open protocol').

title: Post-migration cleanup
summary: Close out the June-migration and August-pivot leftovers now that the monorepo, npm rename, docs site, and org archival are done.

title: contract validate: exit non-zero when validation fails
summary: contractValidateCommand returns { success: ok } (cli/src/commands/contract.ts:497), but the CLI action discards it: `.action((options) => { contractValidateCommand(options); })` (cli/src/cli.ts:~567). A failed validation sets the contract to failed and writes feedback, yet the process exits 0, so CI, scripts, dispatch wrappers and agents that trust the exit code treat a failed contract as passed.

title: TUI: parity with the decision framework
summary: The desktop got a Decisions view and decision details overnight (spec-11/12); the TUI only learned the ● glyph and the type cycle. Bring it level, in the TUI's own idiom (keys, footer, help overlay), reading the same core API (groupDecisionsByPrefix, summarizeDecision, buildDocGraph).

title: MCP parity: every CLI capability has an MCP tool
summary: An agent working through `brainfile mcp` should be able to do everything a person can do at the command line, so it never falls back to the CLI or, worse, edits board files by hand. Today it can't: the desktop chat was asked to add columns and had no tool for it (neither has the CLI: only the TUI edits columns), and an agent dispatched to a task cannot even leave a log note over MCP.

title: Default types and the graph: epic, spec, plan, task, decision
summary: Every document is a file with frontmatter, so the board can be a graph and not only a list. Brainfile ships five types with opinions about what each is for and how they connect. Any other name still works, and can borrow a default's place. This board's own config already says it in prose ("Issues are tasks, larger arcs are epics with parentId children, design work starts as specs, decisions are ADRs"); this makes it the default for every board. spec-11's `decision` type is defined here.

title: Memory: fold recoil into Brainfile (decisions on the board, a local index, one brief)
summary: Recoil (Go, SQLite, one database per machine) keeps agents' decisions, handoffs and an index of project docs. Its memory never leaves the machine it was written on: on the Mac Studio it holds 1,090 indexed doc chunks and not one decision, and `.recoil/` is excluded from git. Brainfile already carries state between machines (the board branch, `refs/brainfile/*`, the field-level merge driver), already has ADRs whose `supersededBy` nothing reads, and both tools install a SessionStart hook. So memory moves into Brainfile, rebuilt on Brainfile's ground rather than ported line for line. Old recoil records are not imported. This replaces adr-2's split ("durable decisions live in ADRs (board) and recoil (lifecycle, supersession)"): both now live on the board.

title: Memory and the graph
summary: Fold recoil's memory into Brainfile on top of opinionated default types that form a graph. spec-12 (default types and the graph) comes first: it defines the decision type that spec-11 (memory: decisions on the board, a local index, one brief) builds on.

title: Outline: children stay under their parent across columns
summary: Today the list nests by parentId only within a column, so a parent in In Progress shows alone while its children sit as roots in Review or Done (epic-2 in In Progress, its specs in Review). Decide: a child stays attached to its parent wherever the child's own column is, and the outline is drawn in the parent's column.

summary: core surveyBoards (checkout folder tracked or not, local board branch, remote tracking refs for the configured board name, worktrees of the board branch outside .brainfile/), counts and last change per board, relation by git ancestry within the branch lineage and by content across homes. locateBoard returns the conflict; brainfile where reports every board; CLI preAction, MCP withBoardCommit and the desktop host refuse writes with a resolving error naming the command. Covers spec-15-1, spec-15-2.

title: spec-15 phase 2: backups as refs, merge-boards and adopt
summary: refs/brainfile/backups/<UTC timestamp> before any replace or merge; brainfile backups / backups restore. merge-boards <ref|path> on the field-level merge with ID collisions renumbered and references rewritten; adopt <ref>; containment adopts without a question. Covers spec-15-3, spec-15-4.

title: spec-15 phase 3: one home for the board branch; migrate --to-branch finishes the job
summary: where/lint report board-branch worktrees outside .brainfile/, prune ones whose folder is gone; migrate --to-branch untracks .brainfile/ on the code branch and adds it to .gitignore in one commit; end-to-end runprism.ai reproduction on scratch repos. Covers spec-15-5, spec-15-6, spec-15-8.

title: spec-15 phase 4: desktop two-boards line and health
summary: The board band says 'Two boards: …' with Use theirs / Merge / Keep this one; health covers two boards, stray worktree, ahead/behind the remote, tracked twice, half-done merge. Covers spec-15-7.

title: Board integrity: one board per repo, detected, merged and backed up
summary: A repo should have one board, and Brainfile should know when it doesn't. runprism.ai (2026-10-12) had two: an old plain-files `.brainfile/` tracked on `main` (7 docs) and the newer `brainfile` branch with the Linear import (19 docs), checked out in a stray worktree under `/private/tmp`. `locateBoard` took the folder in the checkout without looking further, so the desktop showed the stale board as "folder" and the CLI would have kept writing to it; `migrate --to-branch` then failed on the branch being checked out elsewhere. An agent untangled it by hand (compared, backed up into `.git/brainfile-backup-2026-10-12`, adopted the branch, PR #2 to untrack `.brainfile/` on `main`). Nothing was lost, but only because it stopped and asked.

title: Sync health: quiet, true, and in one place
summary: Screenshots 2026-10-12 16:10 and 16:11. The top-right corner says three things about sync at once ("3 waiting to send", "⚡ 10 new", and the band's "synced 6m ago ↑6"), the words mean nothing to a person, and the counts are stale: brainfile where reported nothing waiting on any of the six boards at that moment.

title: Window: remember its size and position and restore them on launch
summary: The desktop app opens large and centered every time. Save the window's bounds (size, position, maximized/fullscreen state) when they change or on close, and restore them on the next launch. If the saved position is no longer on any connected display (monitor unplugged, resolution changed), fall back to the current centered default.

title: Tooltips: two or three words, five at most
summary: Screenshot 2026-10-12 16:14. Tooltips read as prose ("What changed on any board from outside: agents, the CLI, other machines"). Make every tooltip software-plain: what it is or does, 2-3 words, 5 at most when needed ("Changes", "Sync now", "Open in Cursor", "Hide projects  ⌘B"). Keys stay as the kbd suffix. Audit every use:tip and tipWithin in desktop/src/renderer (Titlebar, Sidebar, Workspace, TaskRow, TaskDetail, ChatPop, Dock, HandTo, Settings, DecisionsView, BoardView); longer explanations move into the list or pane they open, never the tip. Add the rule to design.md (Microinteractions, the one tooltip).

title: Test dispatch: add a "Hand-offs" note to the desktop README
summary: A throwaway task to try spec-14 end to end in the dev window: hand it to an agent, let it work in its worktree on dispatch/<task-id>, then merge it from the Review section.

title: Dispatch into a worktree: each hand-off on its own branch
summary: Hand to… runs the agent in the person's working copy (Codex's task-15 fix landed uncommitted on feat/desktop-app), so two dispatches, or an agent and the person, share one checkout. Learned from Orca: give each dispatch its own git worktree and branch (task-15 → brainfile/task-15), with the board still shared through the brainfile branch.

title: Discuss: talk a task over with an agent, and update its spec, before handing it off
summary: A "Discuss" key next to the hand-off key (HandTo) in the task detail. It opens a conversation with an agent about this task, with the task loaded as context, before any work is dispatched.

title: Calm ADHD list view: take the mobile app's list as the reference
summary: A calmer, ADHD-friendly way to read the task list on the desktop, modelled on how brainfile-mobile shows its board. The mobile list is quieter than the desktop's rows (desktop/design.md, Rows): at rest a row is its status box, its title on one line, and at most one signal, the loudest it has. The ID, tags, assignee and everything else wait for the task's sheet. Pressing is a fill, and there are no lines between rows.

title: Discuss: record and update decisions from the chat, with the person's yes
summary: Discuss can only suggest decisions. Its instructions forbid recording them, and its allowed tool list (`DISCUSS_TOOLS` in desktop/src/agents/discuss.ts) leaves out `decide`, `supersede` and `retire`. In task-43's discussion, the person decided to make calm mode the default, against decision-5. The agent could only give them wording to record by hand.

title: Light code review: spec-16 phase 1 (dispatch from the desktop chat)
summary: A very quick, light review of spec-16 phase 1 as merged in 2ad5bc9 (feature commit e7280cc: `git show e7280cc`): the desktop's in-app MCP server (dispatch, runs, stop) and the chat showing hand-offs under the reply.

title: Prevent concurrent dispatches from sharing a task worktree
summary: desktop/src/agents/agents.ts:846 (busy check: desktop/src/agents/desk.ts:91). Two concurrent desk dispatch calls for the same board/task both pass liveOn before either awaits recordDispatch. After the host replies, both call startDispatch without rechecking or reserving the task. prepareWorktree reuses dispatch/<task-id>, so two agents edit and commit in the same checkout, breaking decision-2 and risking lost changes. Reproduced with actual deskTools and a deferred start matching the host-write await: both calls succeed and start two runs. Reserve atomically before awaiting and cover desk/Hand to overlap; release reservation on failure.

title: Make stop cancel a dispatch that is still starting
summary: desktop/src/agents/agents.ts:798-799; stopRun at :964-965 and turn at :664. Dispatch registers a starting run before awaiting open (agent download/ACP initialization/newSession). stop finds sessions only by s.run.id, which is assigned in turn after open returns, so stopping during startup marks the run stopped but cancels/kills no session. open subsequently returns and turn unconditionally sets working and sends the task prompt. The tool has already reported Stopped, yet the agent begins editing; a redispatch or discard after stop can also race the old agent in its worktree. Persist cancellation through startup, close late sessions and never prompt a stopped run. Verified by tracing registration/open/turn and stop; existing desk stop test mocks this lifecycle away.

title: Editors: detection across macOS, Windows and Linux, and terminal editors without Ghostty
summary: Editor links in replies only find apps in /Applications, and terminal editors only appear with Ghostty.

title: GitHub integration: track a repo's issues and offer to turn them into tasks
summary: When a repo's git origin points at GitHub, the desktop app detects it and shows that repo's open issues next to the board. For an issue with no linked task, offer to create a Brainfile task from it (title, body, labels as tags) and keep a link back to the issue so it isn't offered twice.

title: Chat: while an agent works with the chat closed, the key widens into its status line
summary: From Linear's minimised agent window, our way. Scope: chat turns on the board in front (`app.liveAsk`), not hand-off runs, which already show on rows.

title: Custom ACP agents: run any ACP server the person names, the way Zed's agent_servers does
summary: The agents Brainfile can start are a fixed list (`KNOWN` in desktop/src/agents/agents.ts; `AgentId` in desktop/src/shared/api.ts is a closed union: claude, codex, antigravity, cursor, grok). A person who has another ACP server on their machine has no way to use it.

title: Phone link, desktop side: sealed LAN server, pairing QR, bridge to the API
summary: Protocol 1 in brainfile-mobile/docs/link.md. Settings, Phone: link switch, Link a phone (QR + Copy link), linked phones with Forget. A ws server on port 47210 running Noise IK (desktop/src/link/noise.ts, identical to the phone's), bridging the whitelisted calls to the host and agents processes and forwarding projects, board and agent events. New calls: decide, live. Branch feat/phone-link.

title: Phone link, phone side: scan, connect, agents on the board, chat
summary: Protocol 1 in docs/link.md. Settings, Desktop: Link desktop (camera QR or pasted link), Linked/Away, Forget. Connection manager over noise.ts. Desk projects join GitHub ones by owner/name; desk-only boards appear. Via the desk: live run as a row's loudest signal, asks band and sheet, Hand to… and Stop on the task sheet, review summary, a chat key and chat sheet with harness and model pickers. Falls back to GitHub when the desk is away.

title: Add effort level setting to model selector
summary: Instead of a separate effort dropdown, hovering over a model lets you choose its available effort levels in a > submenu. Medium is the default, as it is the most commonly available level.

title: Desktop: remove the board (kanban) view; the list is the one view of work
summary: The desktop's Board tab is the only kanban left: the phone and the TUI read as a list grouped by column. The list already does what the board does (drop a task on a group, Move to…, the status box), and the outline, calm rows and the review moment live only there, so the board costs its own rules (a parent's card showing child boxes across columns) for a layout nobody needs in an agentic backend. Columns stay as a task's stage; only the column layout goes.

title: Calm list: a task an agent is working never sits behind More
summary: In the calm list an open group shows its first three roots and the rest under `N more` (design.md, Calm list; `glance` in format.ts). A task an agent is working — starting, working, or waiting — must stay in the drawn list, never behind `N more`, even when it is past that glance. Its family stays with it, the same way a family is never cut. The glance still holds for every other row. Update the Calm list section of design.md to say so.

title: Mobile linked: models + effort in chat and Hand to…, per task
summary: Bring desktop's model + effort behaviour (task-50, task-51) to the phone when linked. Chat sheet and task sheet Hand to… offer the same agents/models as desktop, with effort as a touch equivalent of desktop's model > effort submenu (no separate effort dropdown), medium as the default where available. The per-task choice follows whatever task-51 decides (default, where the choice lives at dispatch, interaction with the selector) — do not invent a phone-only rule. The chosen agent/model/effort is what the desktop runs and what the run row shows on both devices. GitHub-only mode is unaffected. Plain labels for every level and action (decision-10).

title: Mobile: calm list parity — list-only, working tasks never behind More
summary: Match desktop's current list (task-49 list-only, decision-9; task-43/task-52 calm list, decision-7) on the phone: one list grouped by column, no board view; calm rows with only signals at rest; the glance (first three roots, rest under N more) holds except a task an agent is working — starting, working or waiting — and its family, which never sit behind More. Applies in both linked and GitHub modes where the data exists (live run signal only when linked). Same wording and counts as desktop.

title: Mobile: one look and feel with desktop — tokens, rows, sheets and copy audit
summary: Audit the phone against desktop's current design (desktop/design.md and tokens.css as the source, phone theme.ts as the copy) and close the drift since task-41: Forge planes/ink/accent, IBM Plex Sans and Mono, status boxes, row signals, group headers, task/chat sheets, asks band, review moment, empty and Away states. Keep phone-native conventions (native stack, SF Symbols, haptics) — cohesion is in tokens, type, spacing, signals and words, not in copying desktop layout. Every label says what it does in plain words (decision-10). Deliver a short before/after checklist in the task log; fix drift in this task, split anything large into a follow-up under epic-3.

title: Mobile: final polish with native iOS glass, cards and buttons, keeping desktop's look
summary: The last step of epic-3, after task-54, task-55 and task-56. Use the native iOS surface wherever iOS has one: Liquid Glass on bars, toolbars, sheets and floating controls; native buttons, menus, context menus and sheets; inset cards for grouped content such as settings and a task's details. Keep what makes the phone read as the desktop: IBM Plex Sans and Mono, desktop's tokens for planes, ink and accent, the status boxes, the row signals, the calm list and plain copy (decision-10). Where the two disagree, native wins for chrome (bars, sheets, buttons, menus) and desktop wins for content (rows, type, ink and signals). Check every screen on the simulator against desktop/design.md, then build and install on the iPhone over WiFi with npm run phone.

title: Validate mobile parity work in review (epic-3)
summary: Validate the four review tasks under epic-3 (task-54 models + effort, task-55 calm list, task-56 look and feel/copy, task-57 iOS polish) against their specs, epic-3 scope (linked mode only, GitHub-only unchanged except shared list/look), and decisions decision-7 (calm list), decision-9 (list-only) and decision-10 (plain copy). Check the uncommitted work on brainfile-mobile branch epic-3 and desktop feat/desktop-app: tests pass as logged (phone 125/125, desktop 161/161), link protocol-1 effort feature degrades to an older desk, glance holds for working tasks, tokens/type/signals match desktop/design.md, and native iOS chrome follows task-57's rule (native for chrome, desktop for content). The task is drawn there instead of its column (a completed task with an unmerged branch included); the row shows lines added and removed, and Merge under the pointer, the same Merge as the task pane's. A branch that would conflict stays in its column with 'conflicts' as its signal. Now the agents process writes how many agents are at work to BRAINFILE_DEV_BUSY (set by scripts/dev.mjs), and both the agents swap (main.ts) and the Electron restart (dev.mjs) wait for none, saying so once in the terminal. (2) Merge left the task in Review; merging is the person's yes, so the window completes it (a parent with open children stays, and says so). (3) Hand to... started a child whose dependsOn were still open, and the agent's pickup then refused: the task pane's key waits ('Waits on task-62') and the agents process refuses the same dispatch from the chat. (4) Merge ran no checks: it now runs the contract's validation in the hand-off's worktree first (async, 'Checking...'), merges nothing on a failure, toasts the first line and logs the end of the output on the task for Send back. Checks run on the branch as it is, not with the trunk merged in: that stays task-62.

title: The chat manages the board; code work goes to a hand-off
summary: decision-14. Prompt: ASK_PREAMBLE (agents.ts:1164) ends 'Do not change code unless asked', which leaves the chat able to become a dev environment. It says instead that the chat does not change code or run commands; asked for code work, the agent writes the task or updates the one in context (what it must do, how to check it), dispatches it when the person asked for it done, else says it is ready to hand off; and it reads code freely to write a good task. Enforcement, as Discuss has: applyMode gives chat sessions discussMode (never bypass, read-only when offered), and requestPermission refuses edit, delete, move and execute before anyone is asked, keeping board and desk tools and the brainfile command line (the fallback when MCP is missing). Open: whether read-only git (log, status, diff) stays allowed for the health line's Ask agent. Window, words and structure only (decision-10, tips two or three words): the composer's placeholder 'Ask or tell it something' is vague, so it names what it takes (proposed: 'Ask, or add and change tasks'); under a reply, a task the turn added or changed and did not hand off carries a Hand to… key beside it. title: Merge lands from the worktree: a conflict said before, checks run there, the trunk moved by compare-and-swap
summary: decision-12. Today mergeReview runs git merge --no-ff in the person's own folder and aborts on a conflict (worktree.ts:201-226). Instead: Review says whether the branch conflicts with the trunk now, with git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only (nothing written; git 2.38+). Merge brings the trunk into the branch inside the task's worktree, runs the contract's validation (else the repository's checks), makes the landing commit 'Merge task-N: title' with git commit-tree on the trunk tip and the branch, and moves the trunk with git update-ref <trunk> <new> <old>; if the trunk moved, it starts again from the new tip. One landing at a time per repository. When the person's checkout is on the trunk it follows with git merge --ff-only, which works around uncommitted changes in other files; if the landing touches a file they changed, it waits and names the file. The worktree and branch go once landed, as today. Tests with a scratch repository: the trunk moved meanwhile, a conflict, a failing check, a person's checkout with changes on the trunk.

title: A conflict goes back to the hand-off's agent

The send-back carries the conflicting files, the trunk commits it collided with and the tasks that made them (from 'Merge task-N: title' and the board), and the instruction: keep what both sides meant, commit, run the checks. It goes up to the contract's maxRetries (else once), then stays in Review naming the files. The row and Review say it in plain words (decision-10). The CLI and the phone still name the files and stop.

title: Mobile parity 2: what the desktop gained since epic-3 — merge from the phone, waiting on you, sessions
summary: Since epic-3 closed (2026-10-14 03:00) the desktop gained Ready to merge (task-69), Merge that lands and completes (decision-12, task-63), Waiting on you in the feed, and the dock as sessions (task-46 phase B). The link has not changed since, so the phone cannot see or do any of it. This epic brings it over in linked mode only, keeping task-57's rule: iOS for the chrome, the desktop for the content (Plex, Forge tokens, calm rows, one signal a row, plain copy per decision-10).

title: Link contract v3: features target, pull-request, merge-to and queue; desktop/link.md is the full contract; link:dev answers every new call
summary: The phone reaches the desktop through the link (desktop/src/link: server.ts offers `features` in hello, bridge.ts whitelists the api calls a phone may make with their argument shapes, dev.ts and devReviews.ts are the fake desk `link:dev` the phone is tried against). Today `LINK_FEATURES = ['effort', 'merge']` and the bridge carries 25 calls. Add, each gated on a feature the phone checks in hello:
constraints: A feature missing from hello means the phone's older behaviour: nothing new is required of an old phone or desk
Plain copy in any string the phone shows (decision-10)
Change nothing in ../brainfile-mobile
Do not add queue to LINK_FEATURES or move dispatch status into core: task-123 does

title: Dependencies across boards: a hand-off, a lead and a brief treat alias:task-id as a real dependency, open until it is complete and landed on the related board
summary: A task may depend on one on a related board (`dependsOn: [mobile:task-3]`; `related:` in brainfile.md names the alias and the repo folder; `brainfile show` and the CLI's `relatedBoards(filePath).dependencies` already resolve them). The runtime ignores them: runner.ts ≈866 filters `!ref.includes(':')` from a hand-off's waits, lead.ts ≈162/229/249 drops them from readyOf, the plan and the waves, and brief.ts ≈97 leaves their notes out of leftFor. So tonight's phone epic cannot wait on this epic's contract child by dependsOn; Claude starts it by hand.
constraints: A missing related board counts as an open dependency, said plainly, never as satisfied

title: Link queue: the real desk answers queue(projectId) from core's dispatch status, alias waits included; the feature queue is offered in hello
summary: Split from task-120 by the lead: the `queue` feature of link contract v3, for the real desk. task-120 documents the queue call's shape in desktop/link.md and may give link:dev a fake answer; this child makes the real desk answer it.
constraints: dispatch status from the CLI and MCP says what it said before for boards with no related-board dependencies
A feature missing from hello means the phone's older behaviour
Plain copy in any string the phone shows (decision-10)

title: Link parity test and the epic's whole: every api method is bridged for the phone or excluded with a reason, link:dev answers every bridged call, and the four features work end to end
summary: What keeps the phone from drifting behind the desktop again, and the epic's last child: it wires and tests the whole. cli/src/__tests__/mcp-parity.test.ts maps every CLI command to an MCP tool or an exclusion with a reason; do the same for the link.

title: The task view carries the hand-off record: dispatch (agent, model, by, at, until, tries, the claim held or ended with its outcome) in the snapshot and getTask, in link.md under target, and in link:dev's fixtures
summary: Found by the phone epic's lead (mobile epic-1, 2026-10-16 06:55): the phone's task sheet shows the hand-off record (agent, model, when, by whom; held by a runner or ended with its outcome), but the desk's TaskView (desktop/src/shared/api.ts) and desktop/link.md carry no `dispatch`, so the sheet is empty on a linked board.

title: One system, desk side: the link carries everything the desktop gained since epic-7 (targets, pull requests, the queue), a parity test keeps it that way, and dependencies across boards are honoured
summary: The desk half of bringing the phone level with the desktop, so the two feel like one system: the same words, the same signals, the same actions in the same places, and nothing on the desktop that the phone cannot at least see. The phone half is the epic on the related board `mobile` (../brainfile-mobile), whose children wait on this epic's first child.

title: Make handoffs configurable per task (model + effort)
summary: Related to task-50 (effort level in the model selector). Design is undecided and needs to be determined first: when handing off to Claude, does that always mean a fixed model (e.g. Opus), or can the user select model + effort per task — e.g. Opus xhigh for one task and Sonnet medium for another? Decide the default, where the choice lives at dispatch time, and how it interacts with the model selector's effort submenu (medium default).

title: Show task as full pane on left when chat side pane is open
summary: If a side pane is already open for chat, and the user opens a task, it should show full pane on the left side instead of a floating card.
